rootCauseOneLine: bb keeps one long-lived `claude` CLI process per thread (never recycled after a rate-limit/auth failure), and that process memoizes the OAuth token it loaded at startup, only invalidating it when the mtime of ~/.claude/.credentials.json changes or via a 30 s (stale-on-failure) Keychain cache on macOS; a login the probe cannot see stays pinned until a new process (server restart / thread stop) is spawned.
proposedFix: In plugins/provider-claude-code/src/bridge/bridge.ts, when a turn's SDK result is_error with category rate-limit/unauthorized/billing (error-info.ts), flag the ThreadSession recycle-on-next-input and have getWritableThreadSession treat it like streamEnded: settle, emitSessionReplacement, and start(providerThreadId) a fresh SDK session (existing replaceEndedThreadSession path). The new claude process reads credentials at startup so a login done in between applies on retry; conversation survives via SDK resume; no wire change (no protocol bump). Interim workaround: `bb thread stop <id>` on the idle thread releases the runtime so the next message spawns a fresh process (verified).
caveats: Plain Linux flow (claude login rewrites .credentials.json) does NOT reproduce with Claude Code 2.1.233/2.1.234: the CLI notices the mtime change and reloads on the next request. The pinned-token behaviour was reproduced deterministically only when the store changes without an mtime change (Linux analog of a macOS Keychain login next to a leftover plaintext file, or a failed/timed-out Keychain re-read). macOS could not be run here; the Keychain-cache analysis comes from reading the shipped darwin binaries' embedded JS. Reporter's OS/CLI version unknown; suggested check: `ls -la ~/.claude/.credentials.json` on their Mac and CLI debug logs for "[keychain] read failed; serving stale cache".
